Tuning SQLite

SQLite is a fine engine for a small personal server when its settings match the workload. The write ahead log lets readers keep going while a single writer appends its pages. A busy timeout of a few seconds turns most lock errors into a short and quiet wait. Normal synchronous mode is a fair trade on a machine that rarely loses power. Checkpoints fold the log back into the main file, and their size deserves a glance. Indexes help the.

queries you run every day and slow down the writes you rarely notice. Strict tables refuse a value of the wrong type instead of converting it in silence. Measuring before tuning saves an afternoon of changes that move nothing at all. A fictional benchmark on a modest board shows the gain of each setting in turn.
